evidence: The bitmap contains two independent waveguides with four external ports.
Each guide is routed by S-bends into a long, close, parallel central region.
The parallel region is the function-defining interaction span where evanescent coupling transfers power between the guides.
topology_reasoning.operation: Optical power launched into one input couples to the adjacent guide according to the supermode beat length set by waveguide width, gap, and coupling length; the S-bends only fan the ports out from the close interaction region.
topology_reasoning.implementation_plan: Use primitives only: two gf.Path centerlines smoothed through waypoints and extruded on layer (1,0), plus primitive path tapers/straight sections if needed. All knobs remain top-level assignments in device.py. The script will write lengths.json from the generated path lengths so verify_knob_response can prove coupling_length moves real geometry.

iterations.change_made: Initial two-path directional coupler model with linear port tapers, smoothstep S-bends, top_width=0.36, bottom_width=0.26, coupling_gap=0.16, coupling_length=56.5.
Changed bend centerlines from diagonal smoothstep transitions to sampled Bezier vertical lobes. This underfilled target bend lobes and added inner-arc overdraw, so it was not the best candidate.
Replaced Bezier lobes with target-row-derived bend waypoints while keeping constant guide widths. This improved trajectory alignment but still underfilled broad bend shoulders.
Added tapered bend-width boost primitives over the four S-bend lobes. Recall improved strongly, but lower-left and upper-right bends became red-heavy.
Narrowed lower guide, widened upper guide, and reduced top-right/bottom-left bend boosts. False positives dropped but false negatives increased; iteration 4 remained the best.

Used iteration-4-style upper width, intermediate lower width, moderate top-right/bottom-left boost reductions, shifted top-right bend left, and shifted bottom-left bend right. This was the best candidate after six comparison calls.
